feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. Iteration 0's five-sensor baseline (x ±0.03 m, 12 mm footprints, y 0.06 m) gave 100% off_track ends on all three development tracks, with one line-loss event per run and max_error of 0.060 to 0.068 m. Progress was only 0.105 to 0.158. Together these point to the line leaving the sensors' view at lateral offsets beyond about 0.05 m, not to the body or wheels. Body width cannot help, because the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m for body_width up to 0.18 m. In my controller I had to scale weights to the wider span (weights proportional to x, clipped to ±2) and lower base speed to 1.5, because the 1.8 run drifted off early. I also raised kd to damp oscillation, which was highest on s-bend and slalom in iteration 0 (steering_oscillation 0.147 and 0.160). When the next race reports: if line_loss_events is still about 1 per run and max_error is near 0.06, the span is still too narrow, so push the outer sensors to x ±0.08 m (the contract limit). If the line is held but progress stays under 0.3 with high steering_oscillation on s-bend or slalom, move the forward offset closer to the axle (y 0.04 m) to cut lag. If progress rises but the robot still runs off track on tight bends, the wheel geometry may limit turning rate, so test wheel_track 0.10 m.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stays at about 1 per run with max_error near 0.06 m: widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.08 m (the contract limit), keeping sensor_size 0.016 and the seven-sensor array. Evidence: iteration 0 (all 60 trials ended off_track, max_error 0.060 to 0.068 m, one line loss per run) shows the line leaves the 12 mm, ±0.03 m array before the robot can recover.

If the line is held but steering_oscillation stays high (above about 0.15) on s-bend or slalom: move the forward offset from y = 0.05 m to y = 0.04 m to cut sensor-to-wheel lag. Evidence: iteration 0 had its highest steering_oscillation on slalom (0.160) and s-bend (0.147), and those tracks had the highest max_error.

If progress stays below 0.3 with no line loss on any track: change wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m to raise turning rate, or wheel_radius from 0.03 m to 0.035 m for more ground speed. Evidence: iteration 0 progress was 0.105 to 0.158 on every track, with no line loss in the non-off-track sections, so this would indicate a speed or turning-rate limit rather than a sensing one.
